correspondents: A Venetian secretary → the Venetian ambassador in England

status: Attempted, open (21 Sept 2026; restored 14 Oct 2026 for sp106r722). This entry first held only R703, closed on 21 Sept 2026 as a codebreaker's worksheet on a 'lost' 46-line letter; the letter is R722 (endorsed 'Cypher of a Venetian Secretary to the Embassador of that nation', 1625; Spinola before Breda, the Pope and Bethune in the clear passages). known: R722 identified (Venetian secretary to the ambassador, first half of 1625); endorsement and clear Italian passages read; all 420 code groups transcribed; four values from clear-text junctions and some from the codebreaker's partial key R701 p. 3 (sp106r722.html).

title: Palm (London) to Starhemberg, German letter with ciphered passages, 1727
status: DECODE R7927-R7930 viewed 21 Sept 2026 (targets/palm1727/). R7927 ff.16-17: German letter, mostly clear, 14 passages in a homophonic cipher (2-79) with 3-figure codes; a few groups glossed at the time (33=e 23=n 10=d 15=t 40=long s 230=der). R7928 = Windischgrätz-Starhemberg letter key, does not fit. R7930 f.41 = cover of a Palm-Visconti letter + French/Italian 1-500 worksheet; that letter not imaged. 162 letter tokens: 5-gram annealing failed. Needs Palm's key or the Deciphering Branch clear copy. Narrowed to the unread part and restored 2 Nov 2026.
why: Ciphered despatches of Palm to Visconti / Staremberg, 14 Mar 1727; what the cipher hides is not known.

verify: Search the same volume and the Calendars for the contemporary decipherment first. Fetch the images and the key record(s); test the key on the first lines.

title: Johann Joachim von Rusdorff to Axel Oxenstierna, The Hague, 1628, three letters in cipher (R4333-R4335)
correspondents: unknown → Camerarius?, Amsterdam; Rusdorff → Oxenstierna; Swedish agent → Oxenstierna
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Oxenstierna af Södermöre, Ser. B, E 701 (DECODE R4333-R4335)
status: DECODE R4284–R4341, 8 records in four different ciphers, each its own entry since the one-key split of 14 Oct 2026. Viewed 21 Sept 2026. The two Bremen letters of 1631 (R4330–R4331, riksarkivet1628.html) are read and removed from this entry; R4282 was deciphered by George Lasry (decode4282.html). R4306: contributed partial Dutch decipherment by George Lasry, transcribed with CTTS then solved with Opus 5.5 (17 Oct 2026; sweden4306.html, which also records this project's failed attempt of 21 Sept 2026); pencilled 1632? and Amsterdam attribution remain qualified, four code identities open. R4336–R4337 turned out to be Rusdorff's London letters of February 1625 in a homophonic cipher with an alphabetical nomenclator; key recovered from the ciphertext by George Lasry (21 Oct 2026, PR #72; rusdorff1625.html) and removed from this entry. Open: R4284 (Latin 1628, Camerarius docket; riksarkivet4284.html) — attacked with Latin annealing and against two box keys, not broken; R4333–R4335 (Rusdorff → Oxenstierna 1628, another cipher; rusdorff1628.html) and R4338–R4341 (E 708, Swedish, June 1633, not 1646; glossed in part at the time; oxenstierna1633.html) surveyed only. Narrowed to the unread part and restored 2 Nov 2026.
why: One remaining key-box ciphertext that resisted a first attack, and Oxenstierna correspondence of 1628 and 1633 with a key collection that may hold their keys.

verify: Fetch the images and the key record(s); test the key on the first lines.

R4336-R4337 (Rusdorff, London, Feb 1625) key recovered ciphertext-only by George Lasry with CTTS and Claude Opus 5.5, 21 Oct 2026 (rusdorff1625, PR #72); codes 628 and 701 open.
